A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gradient-testing and estimation work. All 35 pages of v2 and 37 pages of v3, including Appendices A–D, support comparison; equations, algorithms, tables, and figures are readable.

before.justification: v2 reports algorithms, theoretical complexity bounds, and proofs, including in its appendices. Table 1 summarizes theoretical results; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: Section 5, Tables 2–3, and Figure 1 report original numerical experiments measuring correctness, estimation error, comparison-query counts, and optimization convergence.

M1.justification: The core procedures remain, with consequential local corrections. Algorithm 2 adds γ to its probing precision, changes repetitions from ceil(800 ln(1/δ)) to ceil(3200 ln(1/δ)), and changes its threshold from 23/40 to 63/80. Algorithm 4 corrects its binary-search midpoint. v3 also introduces repetition and candidate selection for confidence amplification.

E1.justification: v3 introduces empirical coverage absent from v2: general strongly convex quadratics, sparse quadratics, and extended Rosenbrock functions. Evaluation covers gradient testing, gradient estimation, and optimization using estimated directions.

E2.justification: Figure 1b–c introduces evaluated comparisons against Ideal AdaNGD, ZO-SGD, ZO-RankSGD, and SCOBO. v2 discusses related methods but contains no corresponding empirical comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5 introduces complete evaluation protocols: testing directions at distances 0.95ε and 2.05ε, dimension and precision sweeps, ℓ2-error and query-count measurements, and 200-iteration Rosenbrock optimization with and without line search. These are new experiments, not revisions to earlier experimental settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds dimension and precision sensitivity analyses, a joint regression checking n log(1/ε) query scaling, and a comparison of optimization with versus without line search. v2 contains no corresponding empirical analyses.

E5.justification: v3 first documents 100 trials per accuracy/query-count configuration and convergence averaged over ten random initializations. This adds basic repeated-run and averaging information; confidence intervals, error bars, seed identifiers, and significance tests are not supplied.

E6.justification: All empirical results are new. For Rosenbrock at n=100, Table 3 reports mean error 0.0072 and 925.7 queries at ε=0.2, versus 0.00045 and 1320.7 at ε=0.01. The query-scaling fit has R²=0.999. Section 5 reports a final line-search objective of 0.23 for AdaNGD+Ours, matching Ideal AdaNGD, while the other baselines remain above 10.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 revises its one-sided probability bounds and Hoeffding calculation. Theorems 3–4 add high-confidence guarantees and logarithmic amplification overhead. Appendix A.2 replaces the constant-overlap derivation and changes its explicit error constant from 2.04 to 1.35. Appendix C also corrects the Fourier-transform exponent by including division by T.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s main-results list, and Table 1 retain the same headline query-complexity and optimality claims. The conclusion retains its previous claims. Added experiments and confidence-amplification results do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explains γ as a nondegeneracy condition governing probing radius and discusses alternatives to Haar-random frames. Section 5 adds interpretations concerning conservative worst-case bounds and directional accuracy explaining optimization behavior. The concluding open problems remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly documents Apple M2 hardware with 16 GB memory, synthetic-function construction, γ=0.05 for the query sweep, optimizer step sizes, baseline probe counts, and line-search parameters. These disclosures accompany the new experiments; no code-access information is added.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Chatterjee, Kim and Ramanan, De and colleagues, and Levy, plus the earlier v1 note. A new footnote states that this work subsumes that note. The broader positioning against previous optimization and quantum algorithms remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 adds a numerical-experiments section and localized explanatory paragraphs, rewrites portions of Appendices A.2 and B.2, and reorders nearby algorithm/theorem presentations. Most existing narrative, including the abstract and conclusion, is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds two empirical tables and a three-panel figure showing query counts and convergence. These localized displays introduce new visual evidence; the existing summary table, algorithm-box format, and overall single-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: Algorithm 2’s threshold correction and Algorithm 4’s midpoint correction improve the documented procedures, while Section 5 adds useful empirical checks absent from v2. The gain is limited: the replacement Appendix A.2 derivation unjustifiably identifies m(α_n) with a random sample mean, and the optimization comparisons use only same-order query budgets, restricting their support for practical superiority.
